title: A Echo for the Terminal Again
premise: Orsen Nakamura, the forgotten keeper of a derelict beacon at the edge of the Meridian system, is the only witness to a nine-second gravitational flicker that erased an entire mining colony from every official record. As he digs into the anomaly, he discovers the colony's dead left behind a distributed echo—a backup of their memories hidden inside the beacon itself, commissioned by his own vanished mother. Hunted by the Concord's erasure bureau and betrayed by the one ally he trusts, Orsen must broadcast the massacre to a system that has already decided it never happened. In the end, he sacrifices the beacon—and his anonymity—to seed the echo across ten thousand civilian relays, ensuring the truth survives even as the authorities close in on him.
about_author: Marguerite Vane is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. She writes from a houseboat off the northern coast, where she claims the fog does half her plotting.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Nothing
chapters.summary: Orsen Nakamura performs his quiet routines aboard Beacon 7-Kestrel, logging impossible insurance claims that no one ever reads. His POV establishes a life built on deliberate invisibility. The emotional beat is lonely contentment—until the beacon registers a gravity fluctuation of impossible magnitude, nine seconds long, originating from Colony Verity.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Still Orsen's POV: he replays the sensor data and finds Colony Verity—forty thousand souls—officially never existed. No manifests, no charters, no graves. A cold dread replaces his routine calm as he realizes the flicker wasn't an accident but a weapon's signature, and that someone scrubbed the system clean within minutes.

chapters.title: Claims Adjuster
chapters.summary: Orsen files a routine inquiry through his old insurance network and draws the attention of Investigator Sefa Rhee, a sharp Concord auditor who arrives uninvited. Her POV reveals she suspects him of fraud but senses something deeper. The beat is wary cat-and-mouse: two professionals circling the same lie from opposite sides.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV: following a maintenance thread older than his tenure, he finds a sealed partition in the beacon's core containing fragments of human memory recordings—voices, faces, a child singing. The emotional beat is awe curdling into grief as he realizes the beacon was built to be a tomb for testimony.

chapters.title: Commissioned by N. Nakamura
chapters.summary: The partition's creator signature reads Nakamura—his mother, Ilsa, who disappeared twenty years ago. Orsen's POV fractures between present investigation and flashback memories of her evasiveness. The beat is vertigo: his invisibility was engineered, his posting assigned so he would one day find this.

chapters.title: Sefa's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sefa Rhee's POV: back at Concord Station, she cross-references Orsen's inquiry against a classified erasure order and finds her own name listed as a future signatory—an order dated three days from now. The beat is dawning horror; she realizes she was sent not to investigate but to be complicit.

chapters.title: The Erasure Bureau
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV: a Concord strike team boards the beacon under pretense of inspection while he hides in the memory partition's maintenance shafts. He watches them plant falsified logs. The beat is claustrophobic terror—the first time in his life invisibility fails to protect him.

chapters.title: A Thief of Records
chapters.summary: Orsen escapes to the drift-habitat Crowsnest and contacts Dex Oyelaran, a black-market archivist who deals in deleted histories. Dex's POV introduces the underworld of justice outside the law. The beat is grudging alliance: Dex agrees to help only because the erasure threatens his own buried past.

chapters.title: Voices in the Partition
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV: decrypting more of the echo, he hears the final hours of Colony Verity—protesters, then gunfire, then the gravity weapon. Among the voices is his mother's, recorded alive after her supposed death. The beat is devastating hope: she survived long enough to hide the truth here.

chapters.title: Rhee Defects
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV: refusing to sign the pre-dated order, she goes dark and tracks Orsen to Crowsnest, arriving ahead of the Bureau's kill team. The beat is tense negotiation turned alliance—she offers her credentials and her guilt as weapons, admitting she once signed a smaller erasure herself.

chapters.title: Crowsnest Burns
chapters.summary: Multi-POV action chapter: the Bureau raids the habitat. Dex sacrifices his archive to cover their escape, staying behind with a decoy drive. Orsen's POV carries the grief; the beat is the cost of witness made literal—every person who helps them becomes a target.

chapters.title: The Mother Problem
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV: tracing Ilsa's voiceprint, they learn she was Verity's chief engineer and helped design the gravity weapon before turning whistleblower. The beat is bitter reckoning—Orsen must decide whether the woman who hid him away was a hero or a coward, and whether inheritance means repeating her choices.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV: using her old clearance, she walks into Concord headquarters and interviews the Bureau director under pretext of closing her file. She learns the massacre was ordered to conceal a debt-default experiment: Verity's population was collateral in a financial weapon test. The beat is cold fury.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Relays
chapters.summary: Dex's parting gift surfaces: a map of civilian relay nodes the Bureau cannot scrub in time. Orsen's POV plans the broadcast—but the echo is incomplete without the beacon core itself, meaning he must go back to the place where he is most hunted. The beat is resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Trap at Kestrel
chapters.summary: Orsen returns to Beacon 7-Kestrel, which the Bureau has rigged as bait. Sefa's POV covers the approach run while Orsen infiltrates through the same maintenance shafts he once hid in. The beat is inverted claustrophobia—the hiding places of chapter seven now become his attack routes.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Last Message
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV: deep in the core, he finds a message addressed to whoever found the echo—explicitly to him. Ilsa explains why she erased herself from his life: visibility would have killed them both before the echo matured. The beat is cathartic grief and forgiveness, delivered alone in the dark.

chapters.title: Signatory
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV: cornered by her former partner, Auditor Brannoc, she turns the tables by broadcasting his complicity over open channels, forcing the Bureau to divert forces. The beat is triumphant defiance—justice outside the law wielded by someone who once enforced the law's lies.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax begins, Orsen's POV: he splices the echo into the relay network as Bureau boarding teams breach the beacon. Forty thousand voices flood every public channel in the system—testimony, names, the child's song. The beat is overwhelming release after seventeen chapters of suppression.

chapters.title: The Nine Seconds, Reversed
chapters.summary: Climax continues, alternating POVs: across the system, citizens stop to listen; riots bloom at Concord stations; Sefa holds the relay hub against Brannoc's last assault. Orsen triggers the beacon's self-destruct to prevent recapture of the core. The beat is chaos transformed into momentum.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Witness
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, drifting in a lifepod among debris: the beacon is gone, his home with it, but the echo replicates faster than any purge can follow. Sefa retrieves him. The beat is hollow peace—he won, and winning cost him the only shape his life had ever held.

chapters.title: Trials Without Courts
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV: the exposed directors face tribunals improvised from citizen juries, imperfect and messy—justice outside the law proving both necessary and dangerous. Some guilty walk free; some innocent are scapegoated. The beat is sober maturity: truth was the beginning of justice, not its completion.

chapters.title: An Echo for the Terminal Again
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Orsen's POV: he takes a new post maintaining an ordinary, honest lighthouse-relay, no longer hiding but simply living. A stranger arrives carrying a copy of the echo, asking him to verify it. He signs his full name for the first time in the book. The beat is quiet continuity—inherited purpose, freely chosen.
